newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week October 25 - Nov 1.
**OCTOBER 25**
LONDON - The government plan to bring forward legislation early for the next Parliament to privatise national air traffic services.
LONDON - Virgin Express to offer standard single fare of 32 stg exclusive of taxes on the new London-Brussels service which starts on October 27.
GENEVA - IATA is protesting strongly over a U.S. refusal to clear way for fast compensation for victims of air crashes, accusing Washington of acting "illegally and unwisely."
NEW YORK - The Bulk of USAir Group's claims against American Airlines and BA remain undecided, as a federal judge dismissed only one claim against American Airlines.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong and Hanoi are to be linked by four new evening flights a week under the Cathay Pacific and Vietnam airlines joint venture.
LISBON - TAP-Air Portugal will lease 22 Airbus Industrie medium-haul planes.
PARIS - September 1996 import traffic from the Paris airports, Charles de Gaulle and Orly, totalled 45,169 tonnes, an increase of 7.1 percent on the same month last year.
* September 1996 export traffic totalled 49,954 tonnes, up 1.4 percent on a year ago.
* Jan-Sept 1996 import traffic totalled 383,408 tonnes, an increase of one percent on the same period last year.
* 432, 504 tonnes of air cargo exports left the two Paris airport in the first nine months of 1996, down 1.7 percent on the same period 1995.
GENEVA - Memphis, the base of Fedex, world's busiest cargo airport in Jan-July this year.
NEWARK - Continental will increase flights between New York and Florida to 49 a day between December and March.
* Continental will begin daily non-stop service to Panama City, Panama and Guayaquil, Ecuador from N.J's Newark international airport, starting October 27.
HONG KONG - All three airlines flying directly between Hong Kong and London said they can start to use a new, short cut to Europe across China from October 27 with the start of the winter timetables.

BERLIN - Lufthansa operations manager Gerhard Stoenner told a freight managers congress the air cargo industry will benefit strongly from a wider global spread of industrial production by German companies.
TORONTO - Lufthansa Cargo said it will levy a US$0.10 per kilo surcharge on all freight shipments worldwide, effective November 1.
NEW YORK - USAir Group, determined to expand overseas, soon will be flying solo at a time when most of its competitors are entrenched in international alliances.
CHICAGO - Struggling to stay on course away from its troubled past, TWA must now find a new chief executive to take the helm of the troubled carrier.
BEIJING - China's air freight volume hit 736,000 tonnes in Jan-Aug, up 18.1 percent from a year ago.
JOHANNESBURG - SAA has accused domestic rival Comair of illegal spying into its computer database.
DOHA - Iran Air launch new weekly flight from Doha to the southern port of Bushehr on October 27.
DUBAI - Emirates Airline starts thrice-weekly service to Kuala Lumpur via Dhaka on an Airbus A300-600 aircraft, effective October 27.

WASHINGTON - Senior U.S. and European Union aviation officials are to meet to open what are certain to be a long and arduous talks towards ending the many restrictions now curbing transatlantic air travel.
SINGAPORE - Singapore Airlines expected its passenger traffic to remain strong but added that yields would continue to come under pressure from the strength of the Singapore dollar.
**OCTOBER 28**
JAKARTA - Garuda airlines has launched its first cargo aircraft in a bid to compete with other regional carriers.
* Garuda said it was committed to further investment in the air cargo sector after launching its first cargo flight, and was confident of growth potential in the market.
LONDON - Almost half of British airports lack the most up-to-date security equipment, according to a report published by the government security arm Transec.
BERLIN - Electronic cargo bookings through Internet transport services are likely in the near future, logistics expert Prof. Heinz Isermann forecast to freight manager.
PARIS - Air France and its shareholders will study the possibility of buying AOM airline.
MOSCOW - Transaero will begin scheduled cargo flights from Moscow to Phuket in Thailand and Bali in Indonesia from Dec 5.
VIENNA - Lauda Air planned to raise air fares for scheduled flights by four percent from November 1 in response to higher jet fuel costs.
HONG KONG - Work will start Oct 30 on Cathay Pacific's new HK$1.6 billion headquarters at Chek Lap Kok.
AMSTERDAM - Schiphol airport handled 8.9 percent more airfreight in September.
BEIJING - China National Aviation the main shareholder of Hong Kong's Dragon Airlines, has taken over operations of eastern China's Zhejiang Airlines.
GOLDEN, Colo. - Atlas Air expects to return to "more normalised operations" in the fourth quarter after posting $2.6 million in third quarter chargers to add new aircraft to its fleet.

HONG KONG - Korean Air said there was an 8.4 percent rise in the amount of cargo by weight on both domestic and international flights during July compared with the same period last year and in August there was a 6.3 percent increase.
COPENHAGEN - SAS had static earnings but a three percent rise in spending during the first half of 1996 and would have to increase productivity and freeze employment to restore itself to health.
HONG KONG - Kong Kong Dragon Airlines is increasing its flights to Sendai in Japan from October 29 to six a week from the present four.
* Japan Airlines is expanding its new express cargo service called "J Speed" to meet rising demand for rapid deliveries throughout Asia.
